use: a chart reveal of a surprising number
request: Make a quick video showing how little of Earth's water we can actually drink. Use a visual people get instantly.
topic: How much of Earth's water is in lakes and rivers
intent: A general audience on social media, curious about water scarcity.
goal: The viewer remembers the proportions: almost all water is ocean, most fresh water is ice or underground, and lakes and rivers are a sliver.
promise: All of Earth's water as glasses you can count.
arc: One hundred glasses, ninety-seven turn to ocean, the three fresh ones split, and a tiny sliver remains lit.

events.text: Picture all the water on Earth as one hundred glasses.
events.job: Set up the unit everything is counted in.

events.text: Ninety-seven of them are salty ocean.
That leaves three fresh glasses. How much of that can we actually drink from lakes and rivers?
events.job: Narrow to the fresh water and ask the viewer to guess.
events.waiting: How much of the 3 is lakes and rivers?

holds.does: the three fresh glasses wait, picked out from the rest
holds.shows: How much is lakes and rivers?

withhold.what: the size of the lakes and rivers share

events.text: Two of the three are frozen in ice caps. Most of the last one is underground.
events.knows: 2 of 3 fresh glasses are ice; most of the third is groundwater.
events.look: two glasses turning to ice, the third mostly underground

events.text: Lakes and rivers together hold less than one percent of one glass.
events.knows: Lakes and rivers are under 1% of one glass out of 100.
events.look: a tiny sliver of one glass, lit

holds.does: the sliver stays lit against all one hundred glasses

quiz.q: Out of 100 glasses, how many are salty ocean?
Where is most of the fresh water?
quiz.a: Frozen in ice caps (two of the three glasses).

quiz.q: Where is most of the remaining fresh glass?
How much do lakes and rivers hold?
quiz.a: Less than one percent of one glass (out of one hundred).

quiz.q: Which glass was the lakes-and-rivers sliver taken from?
quiz.a: One of the three fresh glasses, the last one, not the ice ones.

quiz.q: Which glasses were picked out from the rest during the first pause?
During the first pause, was the lakes and rivers share shown?
At the end, what stayed lit against all the glasses?
quiz.a: A tiny sliver of one glass.
